cases.name: 01_empty
cases.notes: No nodes at all: empty snapshot, empty WAL. Exercises the zero-length snapshot layout (always uncompressed, even when the compression flag is set) and the CRC over zero bytes.

cases.name: 02_structural_only
cases.notes: semantic_dims = 0, so the has-semantic flag is clear and node entries carry no sem_coords field at all. A reader that unconditionally reads coordinates will desynchronise here.

cases.name: 03_uncompressed
cases.notes: Baseline: raw snapshot entries, raw WAL entries, semantic coordinates present at full Q64.64 width. The simplest complete file.

cases.name: 04_zstd
cases.notes: The same logical content as 03, with the snapshot stored as a single zstd frame. Proves compressed-snapshot handling in isolation (the WAL is empty after compaction).

cases.name: 05_wal_live
cases.notes: Uncompacted: most state lives in WAL entries that must be replayed over the snapshot. Written with the default flush-every-append, so each compressed WAL block holds a single entry.

cases.name: 06_wal_batched
cases.notes: As 05 but with wal_batch_size = 8, so blocks hold multiple entries. Catches readers that assume one entry per block (see the block framing note in the format spec).

cases.name: 07_deletes_and_updates
cases.notes: Live WAL containing INSERT, UPDATE, SET_META and DELETE ops. The expected state is what survives replay, not what was written — a reader that ignores DELETE will report extra nodes.

cases.name: 08_unicode_keys
cases.notes: Non-ASCII paths (accents, CJK, emoji) and non-ASCII metadata values. Key lengths are byte lengths, not character counts.

cases.name: 09_deep_hierarchy
cases.notes: Deep nesting plus wide sibling fan-out, including nodes created implicitly as ancestors. Snapshot entries are parents-before-children; a reader must not assume any stronger ordering.

cases.name: 10_gacl
cases.notes: Access bands encoded into the reserved semantic dimensions and the GACL flag set in the header. Readers are expected to surface the raw coordinates; enforcement is cooperative and out of scope for a reader.

cases.name: 11_meaning_addressed
cases.notes: Format v3: snapshot entries in pure global-Hilbert order rather than depth order. Requires an uncompressed snapshot. A reader must reconstruct the hierarchy from the keys alone.

cases.name: 12_quantized
cases.notes: Format v4: user dimensions stored as TQ1.9 at 2 bytes each. The dumped coordinates are the DECODED full-width values, so a conforming reader must implement dequantisation.

cases.name: 13_epochs
cases.notes: EPOCH markers (op 0x06) interleaved with data ops, including a speculative seal. Markers change no node state; a reader that treats them as node ops will corrupt its replay.

cases.name: 14_history_sidecar
cases.notes: Compacted with Archive retention, so the pre-fence WAL span is archived into a .h000001 sidecar. The main file must be fully readable on its own; the sidecar is optional history.

cases.name: 15_torn_tail
cases.notes: A valid file with a truncated final WAL entry appended. Recovery must stop at the first bad CRC and keep every preceding entry — the expected state is the post-recovery state, and the file is left torn on purpose.
